labels.reason: Historical reviewer: Pattern fires on ordinary English negation that carries no rhetorical reframing: technical descriptions ('The pictures aren't bright enough'), factual corrections with supporting evidence ('The iPhone is not and never was a phone' — a quoted technical critique), plain conditionals ('There does not need to be universal alignment'), standard connectives ('not only makes later rounds harder'), common intensifiers ('nothing short of a phenomenon'), and practical advice ('Be direct, but not mean'). The rule cannot distinguish slop reframing ('It is not X, it is Y — and that makes all the difference') from normal use of negation in analytical prose.
